analysis: Patient with obesity, former smoker, and ECOG 1 develops severe neutropenia (day 15-17), thrombocytopenia (day 77-92), lipase elevation (day 62-70), and bronchiolitis (day 107-112) with systemic edema. This suggests multi-organ toxicity likely from experimental therapy, with pulmonary, hematologic, and pancreatic involvement. The progression from manageable alopecia to life-threatening cytopenias and respiratory compromise indicates high disease burden and poor therapeutic reserve.
evidences: Grade 4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia indicating severe bone marrow suppression
Grade 3 lipase elevation suggesting pancreatic injury
Progressive respiratory symptoms (cough, dyspnea, bronchiolitis) with hemoptysis and systemic edema
